name: Sunset Beach
title: Artificial Turf in Sunset Beach, NC | TIMELESS Grass & Greens
description: Sunset Beach wants a stormwater design once impervious coverage grows by more than 200 sq ft, and caps home lots at 45%. Plan your turf around both.
h1: Turf in Sunset Beach, planned around the Town’s 200-square-foot rule.
lede: Add more than 200 square feet of impervious coverage in Sunset Beach and the Town wants a stormwater design. Home lots top out at 45%. We measure your yard for free, then give you a custom layout and a written price built around both numbers.
wins: Turf area in square feet, ready for the Town
Base depth and any fill written into the scope
A turf edge kept out of the 30-foot buffer

answer.question: Do I need a permit for artificial turf in Sunset Beach?
answer.answer: Ask the Town before work starts. Its UDO requires a zoning permit for any activity that increases impervious square footage, and a Town Fill and Grade permit before a lot is graded, filled or excavated. If the Town counts your turf as impervious and it adds more than 200 square feet, you also need a stormwater design. On a marsh or waterway lot, ask the Town’s CAMA officer too.

blocks.h2: Two numbers set the size of your job: 200 and 45.
paras: The Town of Sunset Beach lists three limits on its Stormwater Requirements page (checked September 2026). New construction and additions of more than 200 square feet of impervious coverage need a stormwater design. Impervious coverage is capped at 45% of the lot. Adding more than 4 inches of fill to any part of the lot needs a Brunswick County stormwater plan.

The Town’s Unified Development Ordinance, adopted September 5, 2023 and amended since, fills in the detail. The 45% cap covers single-family and duplex lots. The conservation and agricultural-forestry districts (CR-1, CR-2 and AF-1) allow 20%. The stormwater plan is due before permits are issued, and a professional engineer, registered landscape architect or surveyor must design it.

Whether turf spends that budget depends on how the Town classifies it. The UDO treats an alternative material as pervious when a North Carolina professional engineer certifies, in a letter under seal, that it meets a hydraulic conductivity of 1.41 inches per hour or more. For scale, the Town’s stormwater page puts an average lawn at about 2 inches per hour. State law on draining turf is covered in our built-upon area guide. Ask the Town which documents it wants before you count on either route.

blocks.h2: Line up the Town’s permits before the old lawn comes up.
paras: Inside town limits, Sunset Beach handles zoning, flood, building inspection and CAMA review itself, according to Brunswick County’s jurisdiction table. Stormwater is shared. The table lists the Town, but the County’s Stormwater Ordinance page says it administers that ordinance in Sunset Beach under an agreement.

Under the UDO, any activity that proposes to increase impervious square footage needs a zoning permit, and site disturbance can’t start until the UDO Administrator issues it. No lot may be graded, filled or excavated without a Town Fill and Grade permit either. On a single-family or duplex lot, you don’t need a scaled grading plan when fill stays at 4 inches or less. Work under that permit must be finished within 90 days.

A turf base is dug, graded and sometimes built up, so take your layout to Planning & Zoning and ask which of these permits your yard needs. Staff meet property owners, and appointments are recommended. If the Town asks for an as-built survey, it must show impervious percentages, including inside any CAMA Area of Environmental Concern.

Seaside, off Seaside Road, sits inside this same review. The Town's approved subdivisions and site plans list shows The Townes at Seaside approved, with its entrance off Seaside and clearing underway, so the 200-square-foot trigger, the 45% cap and the zoning and Fill and Grade permits above reach that ground. Some parcels along Seaside Road sit outside town limits; if yours does, the unincorporated Brunswick County rules on our Grissettown page apply instead. Ask Planning & Zoning which side of the line your parcel falls on before you plan the layout.

blocks.h2: Leave the 30 feet nearest the water out of the plan.
paras: Lots on the marsh or a waterway answer to a state coastal rule as well. Under 15A NCAC 07H .0209, as amended effective November 1, 2025, the estuarine shoreline Area of Environmental Concern runs 75 feet landward of normal high water, or 575 feet beside Outstanding Resource Waters. Impervious surfaces may not exceed 30 percent of the part of the lot inside it. New development must sit 30 feet back from normal high water, with a short list of exceptions.

Artificial turf is not on that list. The list does include grading, excavation and landscaping with no wetland fill. But in September 2021 the Coastal Resources Commission voted 10 to 1 to prohibit artificial turf within the 30-foot buffer, Coastal Review reported, and state staff had required its removal in the enforcement cases they handled. The commission’s August 2025 agenda still carried a variance request for artificial turf within the buffer in Carolina Beach.

The Town’s Building Inspections department includes a CAMA Local Permit Officer. Under the UDO, that officer decides CAMA minor permits, while general and major permits go to the state Division of Coastal Management. Before you settle on a layout, ask where the Area of Environmental Concern and the 30-foot line fall on your lot. We draw the turf edge to that line.

blocks.h2: What the UDO says about fabric, rubber and fences.
paras: Only landscaping fabric that lets rain water flow through is allowed, and solid plastic cover is prohibited. Check that the fabric named in your written scope drains.

The UDO keeps manmade mulch, including recycled tire mulch and other rubberized products, out of the beach districts (BR-1, BR-2 and BB-1), CR-1 and at least 30 feet from any water body. It doesn’t say whether rubber infill under turf counts. If you want rubber in any form, ask Planning & Zoning first.

Fencing a dog area? The UDO requires a zoning permit for fences, and the Town takes fence applications online. Fences in the BR-1, BR-2 and CR-1 districts stop at 4 feet, and mainland residential districts allow 6. Any fence facing the ocean, a waterway, marsh, a lake or a golf course may not exceed 4 feet and must be at least 50% transparent. Our Grand Strand pet turf page covers the dog area itself.

blocks.h2: Take numbers to Town Hall, not guesses.
paras: At the free visit, we measure the area you want to change and check the ground: where water sits after rain, how deep the base goes and whether it adds fill. The custom layout you approve before work starts shows the turf area in square feet. You can set it against the 200-square-foot trigger and your lot’s 45% cap.

In a golf or association community, check its rules as well; our Grand Strand putting greens page covers how several communities treat backyard greens. With the approvals in hand, we prepare the site, build a base for your soil, lay, seam and edge the turf, add infill, clean up and walk you through the care it needs.

servicesNote: A lawn, a dog area or a backyard green, each laid out to fit the Town’s coverage limits.

faq.q: Do I need a tree permit to clear room for turf in Sunset Beach?
faq.a: Not for the tree itself on a lot occupied by a single-family or two-family home, according to the UDO posted on the Town’s server (checked September 2026). Grading, excavation and stump removal still fall under the Town Fill and Grade permit, so tell Planning & Zoning about any stumps in the turf area.

faq.q: When does Brunswick County get involved?
faq.a: Beyond the 4-inch fill rule, the County’s stormwater permit covers residential development that disturbs more than an acre, and any related disturbance within 30 feet of the banks of a natural stream or water body. If your yard backs onto a creek or pond, ask the County’s stormwater staff whether your plan needs that permit.

faq.q: Can I ask for a variance to put turf in the shoreline buffer?
faq.a: The Town’s CAMA Permitting page sets out the route. You need a permit decision first. The petition goes to the Division of Coastal Management Director and the State Attorney General’s Office six weeks before a Coastal Resources Commission meeting. You must show hardship from conditions peculiar to the property that you didn’t cause.

faq.q: Is Seaside part of the Town of Sunset Beach?
faq.a: Some of it is. The Town’s approved subdivisions and site plans list shows The Townes at Seaside approved for construction, which puts that ground under the Town’s zoning permit, Fill and Grade permit and stormwater rules above. Other parcels along Seaside Road can sit outside town limits, where Brunswick County’s rules apply instead, so confirm your parcel with Planning & Zoning before you plan the layout.
